title: Gorgias Pricing (2026): Plans, Tickets and Overages
summary: Gorgias pricing charges per ticket monthly, with overage fees above limits. Estimate costs by calculating peak volumes and comparing to plan allowances.
body_markdown:
## Cutting avoidable tickets with Activepieces beside Gorgias


What Activepieces changes is not what Gorgias charges but how many billable tickets reach Gorgias in the first place.


Its core is MIT-licensed, with 746 integrations counted in the open source monorepo on GitHub, and if you describe an order-status lookup across Shopify and Slack in its built-in chat, what comes out is a live flow in your account, the same kind a builder would assemble by hand, with a run trace for every execution showing exactly what it did to each message.


Its flows run on triggers, branches and schedules across connected apps such as Shopify, Slack and email, and each run costs 1 credit however many steps it has.


The whole arrangement is one flow among the unlimited flows every Activepieces plan includes, the free one too.


What's worth catching depends on where contacts come from.


According to[Open](https://www.open.cx/blog/ai-for-ecommerce) , **order status accounts for 35% of ecommerce contacts** , which means more than a third of your volume is customers asking where a parcel is, a question your Shopify data can answer without an agent.


One in five contacts needs a process, not a conversation: returns and refunds make up 20%, so you'll need a second system for one-fifth of your support work. Shipping adds 10%, and everything else is the remaining 35%.


That last group is the only part that reliably needs a human, so roughly 65% of contacts are candidates for deflection or enrichment before Gorgias counts them.


### A ticket-count alert before the limit


Gorgias bills per ticket, and the invoice arrives after the cycle closes. Where Gorgias's API allows it, an Activepieces flow can call the Gorgias API on a schedule, count tickets created since the cycle began, and post the running total to a Slack channel.


Run once a day, that is about 30 runs a month, or roughly 30 of the 1,000 credits the Free plan includes.


Set the alert at a share of your plan's included volume, such as 80%, and you learn about the overage while there's still time to act, preventing mid-month cost surprises. Without it, the first signal is the invoice.


### Routing noise before it becomes a ticket


Email is where avoidable tickets multiply. A flow can read the inbound message, look up the order in Shopify and, for an order-status question, reply to Slack or the customer with tracking details instead of opening a ticket.


> Email is where avoidable tickets multiply.


Only messages that match nothing are forwarded to Gorgias. Given that order status is 35% of contacts, even a partial catch rate takes a visible share off the count, leaving your contact count dependent on order status completion.


It needs maintenance, and that is the limit of this approach: each rule you write is one more thing to check when a message is misrouted.


What follows is a decision about which categories you trust a flow to answer, and which must always reach a person.
